title.narrative: Institutional Capacity Enhancement for Public Expenditure Management IDF Grant

description.narrative: The IDF grant responds to the Government#s request for assistance in strengthening institutional capacity for deepening the policy content of the annual budget process through strengthening the MTBF and its linkage with the annual budget. Proposed assistance is harmonized with the on-going TA in other PEM areas and will be supporting a Government-owned PEM reform agenda. The timing of the IDF grant implementation will be aligned to the 2006 and 2007 budget cycles, 2007-2009 MTBF process and the second round of National Poverty Reduction Strategy preparation process. Grant is organized in three main components: Component A: Capacity building in the MOF, through two Sub-components: A1. Training for the MOF sector budget analysts in sectoral budget formulation. A2. Building technical capacity in the Budget Department of the MOF to identify and start addressing the deficiencies in data management processes underlying budget preparation. Component B: Capacity Building in the Ministry of Education (MOE) and the Ministry of Transport (MOT) through two Sub-components: B1. Building technical capacity in the MOE and the MOT to identify and start addressing the critical gaps in their information management systems. B2. Building analytical capacity in the MOE and the MOT to focus their spending proposals on key policy priorities and to assign costs to the proposals. Component B focuses on two of the five pilot sectors for the MTBF, the education and transport sectors because: (i) these sectors have a key role in achieving growth and poverty reduction objectives; (ii) these sectors have achieved some progress in moving toward budget preparation in the Medium Term Budget Framework, but costing of the policy priorities and prioritization of the spending remains at a rudimentary stage; (iii) the Bank provides assistance to both sectors through a number of investment projects and the complementary TA is needed to support the policy orientation of the sectoral spending; (iv) other three pilot MTBF line ministries already receive substantial support from other donors for enhancing budget formulation. Component C: Institution building support to the top level decision-makers responsible for formulating sectoral aspects of public expenditure and their technical support staff to enhance their understanding of modern, results oriented budgeting techniques. This will be achieved through study tours and exposure to leading international experts on the political dimensions of modern budget management. The purpose of the Grant is to support the Government of the KR in strengthening its institutional capacity for deepening the policy content of the annual budget process through strengthening the medium term budget framework and its linkage with the annual budget.
